stem: Among people with acute hepatitis C, what proportion will develop chronic hepatitis C?

options.label: A
options.misconception: Treats chronic hepatitis C as rare when it is the usual outcome.
options.explanation: Chronic infection is the common outcome of hepatitis C, not a rarity; more than half of acute infections persist.

options.label: B
options.misconception: Applies the low adult hepatitis B chronicity rate to hepatitis C.
options.explanation: Roughly 5% or less is the rate at which adult-acquired hepatitis B becomes chronic; hepatitis C persists in more than half of acute cases.

options.label: C
options.misconception: None — more than half of acute hepatitis C infections become chronic.
options.explanation: NIDDK states that more than half of people with acute hepatitis C will develop chronic hepatitis C, in which the virus stays in the body.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Underestimates how often acute hepatitis C becomes chronic.
options.explanation: One in five understates it; most people with acute hepatitis C do not clear the virus, and more than half develop chronic infection.

options.label: E
options.misconception: Assumes most people clear hepatitis C spontaneously.
options.explanation: About a third understates chronicity; more than half of people with acute hepatitis C go on to chronic infection.

context: Learning objective: More than half of people with acute hepatitis C develop chronic hepatitis C, a long-lasting infection in which the virus stays in the body.
